title: Tool Authorization & Data Protection
description: Study object-level authorization, secrets and credential handling, output encoding and unsafe rendering, and data minimization and retention. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Object-level authorization
lessons.description: Write an object-ownership check and a denied-access test.
lessons.conceptOverview: Check whether the current principal may access the specific object requested, not merely whether they can call the endpoint. Apply the check inside the service handling the action.
lessons.whyItMatters: Endpoint access does not imply access to every object.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Check whether the current principal may access the specific object requested, not merely whether they can call the endpoint. Apply the check inside the service handling the action.

sections.title: Concept

keyTakeaways: Endpoint access does not imply access to every object.

lessons.title: Secrets and credential handling
lessons.description: Map where secrets can enter logs and define redaction and rotation procedures.
lessons.conceptOverview: Keep credentials outside prompts, retrieved documents and ordinary logs. Use scoped credentials and rotate exposed secrets; redacting the final answer does not undo upstream disclosure.
lessons.whyItMatters: Secret protection must cover internal artifacts and traces.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Keep credentials outside prompts, retrieved documents and ordinary logs. Use scoped credentials and rotate exposed secrets; redacting the final answer does not undo upstream disclosure.

lessons.title: Output encoding and unsafe rendering
lessons.description: Specify safe rendering and explain why input sanitization alone is insufficient.
lessons.conceptOverview: Generated text remains untrusted when rendered or passed to interpreters. Encode for the output context and avoid executing generated HTML, shell fragments or SQL without a constrained interface.
lessons.whyItMatters: Output handling must respect the destination's execution rules.

lessons.title: Data minimization and retention
lessons.description: Create a data inventory and a deletion verification checklist.
lessons.conceptOverview: Collect only data needed for the task and define retention for prompts, outputs, traces and embeddings. Deletion workflows need to include derived artifacts and backups under the applicable policy.
lessons.whyItMatters: Derived artifacts belong in retention and deletion planning.
